title: Orchid: staged heuristic kernel allocator for arch/seq-len mixtures
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem:
Mixed customer workloads (chat + long-document summarization + short quick-completions) show large variance in per-request optimal kernels. Current single-path heuristics pick kernels that are either latency-optimized (bad for long-prefill memory locality) or compute-optimized (worse tail latency for short decode). We need a compact, low-overhead allocator that adapts per-request using lightweight phase fingerprints and safe fallback behavior.

Proposal (Orchid allocator):
- Build a two-stage heuristic: (1) micro-probe fingerprint during first prefill steps to classify request into a small set of archetypes (short-prefill, balanced, long-prefill-high-attn), (2) allocate a kernel bundle using a cost model that combines arch profile (GPU family / SM occupancy), sequence-length bucket, attention width, and tenant policy (latency vs cost).
- Add a staged warmstart: seed the allocator with per-tenant historical distributions (warm buckets) and a small on-host probe cache for recent token length histograms.
- Attention heuristics: detect high-attention-density layers (wide attention matrix use) and prefer kernels with blocked-matmul/attention tiling that reduce memory traffic. For low-attention or sparse patterns prefer fused fast-paths.
- Prefill/Decode scheduling: when prefill classification indicates long KV lifetime, prefer kernels that amortize KV layout costs; for bursty decode-heavy flows prefer low-latency kernels and increase aggressive batching tolerance.
- Safety & rollback: set a conservative safety margin for any kernel change. If measured request latency deviates >15% from predicted, roll back the kernel for that session and flag for retraining the cost model.

Success criteria / metrics:
- Median per-token latency improvement >= 8% on mixed benchmark (balanced test harness).
- P95 tail latency improvement >= 10% for short-decode-heavy workload without increasing cost per token by >5%.
- Change detection and rollback rate < 1% of requests in steady state.

Implementation plan:
1) Design: detailed cost model and fingerprint schema (this ticket).
2) Prototype: allocator library + micro-probe hook in runtime; unit benches across GPUs.
3) Canary: roll out to a small fraction of hosted API (per-tenant canary) with double-write telemetry.
4) Iterate: refine buckets and warmstart seeding, add ML-directed bandit if heuristics plateau.

Trade-offs considered:
- Heuristic simplicity vs model-driven bandit: prefer a small deterministic rule set for initial rollout to keep deterministic rollback and explainability.
- Probe overhead: micro-probe limited to first 6-12 tokens to avoid added steady-state latency.
- Per-tenant state: warmstart improves accuracy but adds storage and privacy concerns; store only aggregated histograms and clear on request.

Notes on scope: this ticket covers the allocator design, metric definitions, and a minimal prototype. Integration into autoscaler and dedicated scheduler is tracked in follow-ups.
updates: 2025-11-04: Ticket created and triaged. Marked P1 due to multiple customer reports of inconsistent latencies on mixed workloads.
2025-11-07: Architecture review with Runtime and Ops. Decided on two-stage approach (probe + cost model) to minimize persistent per-request overhead.
2025-11-10: Prototype micro-probe implemented in local runtime dev branch (orchid/probe). Probe cost measured at ~0.6ms median on A100 for first 8 tokens.

2025-11-12: Benchmark run v1 against mixed workload harness (50% short chat, 30% long prefill, 20% mid-length). Orchid allocator config A shows median per-token -9.4% and p95 -12.1% compared to baseline kernel picker. Cost delta +2.2% token-dollar.
2025-11-14: Design review feedback: add explicit attention-density flag and safety rollback threshold tuning. Also requested per-tenant privacy doc for warmstart histograms.

2025-11-16: PR opened for prototype (github.com/redwood/runtime PR #1234). Added telemetry schema and canary plan. Identified blocker: quantized-kernel signatures not consistently exposed by current kernel registry (ENG-712908 dependency).

2025-11-18: Bench v2 with attention-density heuristic enabled shows improvement for long-prefill workloads (median -6.8% further) and reduced rollback incidents in synthetic stress. Next: prepare canary and Confluence design doc for approvals.
